description: Tier 2 diagnostic. What is connected to the network, and what does ISE know about it? Inventory and profiling first, then composition, then the live attribute detail. The devices themselves are on the Network devices dashboard.

panels.description: Total endpoints in the ISE endpoint database. This is the inventory count, not the live session count — the difference between the two is the estate that is currently switched off.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: (ise3_endpoints_total) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="endpoint_inventory"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="endpoint_inventory"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="endpoint_inventory"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="endpoint_inventory"} == 1))) == 1))

panels.title: Endpoints

panels.description: Endpoints whose session says a posture agent applies to them. The denominator behind every compliance figure on the posture dashboard: a number well below the endpoint total means most of the estate is outside posture entirely.

defaults.noValue: no data — stale, see Collection pipeline

targets.expr: sum((ise3_endpoints_posture_applicable{applicable="yes"}) and on() (((max(ise3_dataset_up{dataset="endpoint_inventory"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="endpoint_inventory"} == 1))) == 1) and ((max(ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset="endpoint_inventory"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset="endpoint_inventory"} == 1))) == 1)))

panels.description: Share of this dashboard's own datasets that both collected successfully and are inside their freshness window (endpoint_inventory, network_devices). Below 100% means some panel here is blank or stale, and the pipeline dashboard says which.

targets.expr: avg(((max by (dataset) (ise3_dataset_up{dataset=~"endpoint_inventory|network_devices"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset=~"endpoint_inventory|network_devices"} == 1))) == bool 1) * ((max by (dataset) (ise3_dataset_fresh{dataset=~"endpoint_inventory|network_devices"} and on(dataset,provider) (ise3_dataset_provider_active{dataset=~"endpoint_inventory|network_devices"} == 1))) == bool 1))

panels.title: Data trustworthy

panels.description: Time since the least recently collected of this dashboard's datasets last succeeded. Every number on this page is at least this old; a value climbing past its collection interval means ISE is answering slowly or not at all.

panels.description: Purpose, reading order, and where to go next. Kept with the dashboard so the meaning cannot drift away from the panels.

options.content:
**Purpose** — describe what is connected to the network and what ISE knows about it — the inventory view, not the incident view.

**Read it in this order**

1. Read the endpoint counts and the unprofiled share.
2. Use the composition tables to check the estate matches expectation.
3. For anything about the switches and routers themselves — which are failing, which are silent, who owns them — go to the Network devices dashboard; this one is about what connects to them.

**When something is red**

- Growing unprofiled count: check the profiling feed before changing policy.
- Blank attribute panels: the detail cache is still filling, see the coverage panel on the Network devices dashboard.
- Endpoint total stepping without a matching import: read the change annotations before treating it as growth.

**Related dashboards** — Triage, RADIUS access, Network devices, Posture, Capacity

*Owner: set this to the team that answers the page. Runbook: link it here — a red panel with no runbook is a puzzle, not an alert.*
